name: Doctor On Demand
one_liner: Major telehealth platform (part of Included Health) with 24/7 access to psychiatry, therapy, and primary care for 98M+ Americans.
short_description: Doctor On Demand by Included Health is a comprehensive telehealth platform offering 24/7 video visits with psychiatrists, therapists, and primary care doctors.
long_description: Doctor On Demand is a leading telehealth platform that merged with Grand Rounds in 2021 to form Included Health. The platform provides 24/7 video visits for urgent care, primary care, therapy, and psychiatry to over 98 million Americans through employer and insurance benefits. Psychiatrists average 15+ years of experience and provide evaluations, medication management, and treatment for anxiety, depression, and other mental health conditions. The platform maintains a 4.9/5 app store rating and offers same-week psychiatric appointments. Doctor On Demand accepts most major insurance plans including BCBS, UHC, Humana Military, Premera, and Medicare Part B. Self-pay options are available for those without coverage.

not_for: Patients needing controlled substances (ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines)

faqs.a: For the 98 million+ Americans covered through employer or insurance benefits, Doctor On Demand visits are often $0. Without coverage, self-pay rates are $99 for medical, $134 for therapy, and $299 for initial psychiatry visits.

faqs.q: Can Doctor On Demand prescribe ADHD medication?
faqs.a: No, Doctor On Demand psychiatrists cannot prescribe controlled substances including ADHD stimulants (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse), benzodiazepines (Xanax, Klonopin), or sleep medications (Lunesta).

faqs.q: What is the relationship between Doctor On Demand and Included Health?
faqs.a: Doctor On Demand merged with Grand Rounds in 2021 to form Included Health. Doctor On Demand continues as the consumer-facing telehealth brand within the Included Health portfolio.

faqs.q: Does Doctor On Demand accept Medicare?
faqs.a: Yes, Doctor On Demand is in-network with Medicare Part B for eligible telehealth services, along with BCBS, UHC, Humana Military, and Premera.
